# UX Checklist: Ticket Management Web UI

**Purpose**: Validate that UX-relevant requirements in spec.md are complete, unambiguous, consistent, measurable, and cover all flows/edge cases — before planning begins.
**Created**: 2026-09-25
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are requirements defined for what information is visible per ticket row in the list view (beyond title/status/priority/assignee), e.g. category or timestamps? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001]
- [ ] CHK002 Are requirements defined for how search/filter input is presented (e.g. always visible vs. expandable, single combined control vs. separate)? [Gap]
- [ ] CHK003 Are requirements defined for the ticket detail view's overall layout/prioritization (e.g. which fields appear above the fold vs. below)? [Gap]
- [ ] CHK004 Are requirements defined for how the edit form is entered/exited (e.g. inline edit vs. separate mode, and what happens to unsaved changes on navigation away)? [Gap, Spec §User Story 4]
- [ ] CHK005 Are requirements defined for visual/textual distinction between a ticket's read-only detail state and its edit-in-progress state? [Gap]
- [x] CHK006 Are requirements defined for confirming a status transition before it is submitted (e.g. a confirm step) versus applying it immediately on selection? [Gap, Spec §User Story 6] — Resolved: User Story 6 Scenario 2 explicitly separates "selects a valid next status" from "and confirms" as two distinct steps before "the transition is submitted."
- [ ] CHK007 Are loading-state requirements defined for the list view, detail view, and form submissions while waiting on the backend? [Gap]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK008 Is "clear 'no tickets found' state" defined with specific required content (e.g. message text, whether it differs for "no tickets exist" vs. "no matches for this filter")? [Clarity, Spec §User Story 1 Scenario 5]
- [ ] CHK009 Is "clear 'ticket not found' message" specified with what the user can do next (e.g. link back to list) or is that left open? [Clarity, Spec §User Story 3 Scenario 4]
- [ ] CHK010 Is "clear, specific 'couldn't reach the server' message" defined with what "specific" means here (e.g. must it distinguish timeout vs. connection failure)? [Ambiguity, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK011 Is the searchable-picker interaction for assignee (FR-005a) specified precisely enough to know what "searchable" requires (e.g. filter-as-you-type vs. simple dropdown scroll)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005a] — Resolved: "searchable picker (combobox)" is a well-understood, unambiguous UI pattern name; FR-005a's companion requirement to accept typed values not yet in the list only makes sense with filter-as-you-type behavior.
- [x] CHK012 Is "no assignees yet — type a name to add one" state's exact trigger condition unambiguous (empty backend list vs. backend list temporarily unavailable)? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-005c] — Resolved: FR-005c's trigger is explicitly scoped to "the known-assignees list is empty," a distinct, definite condition from a failed/unavailable request (which falls under the separate network-error handling in Edge Cases).

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK013 Are empty-state requirements worded consistently across the three cases that need them (empty/filtered ticket list, zero comments, empty assignee list)? [Consistency, Spec §FR-014, §FR-005c] — Resolved: all three follow the same "explicit, distinct state instead of blank/broken" pattern (FR-014 groups the first two under one rule; FR-005c mirrors it for assignees); exact copy is left to implementation by design, consistently, for all three.
- [x] CHK014 Are "specific field-level reason" requirements for backend rejections consistent between creation (User Story 2), editing (User Story 4), and comments (User Story 5)? [Consistency, Spec §FR-012] — Resolved: FR-012 explicitly unifies "creation, edit, comment, or transition" under one rule; no per-story variation exists.
- [x] CHK015 Do the assignee-picker requirements in User Story 2, User Story 4, FR-005a, and Key Entities all describe the same combobox behavior without contradiction? [Consistency, Spec §FR-005a] — Resolved: cross-checked all four references; each describes the identical "backend-sourced searchable picker + typed-value fallback" behavior with no contradiction.

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK016 Can "shows a clear ... state" (used for not-found, empty-list, no-comments, no-assignees) be objectively verified, or does it need a concrete content/format requirement to be testable? [Measurability, Spec §FR-014] — Resolved: while "clear" itself is a soft descriptor, the operational, falsifiable claim (a distinct explicit state renders, not a blank/broken area) is directly testable via presence/absence, independent of exact wording.
- [ ] CHK017 Is SC-001's "without external help" criterion objectively measurable, or does it need a more concrete proxy (e.g. no documentation consulted, first-attempt success)? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001]
- [x] CHK018 Is SC-005's "single action" criterion measurable across both the status-filter and keyword-search interactions, given they may be two separate UI controls? [Measurability, Spec §SC-005] — Resolved: SC-005's own parenthetical ("one filter selection and/or one search submission") already disambiguates this per interaction type.

## Scenario Coverage

- [ ] CHK019 Are requirements defined for what the list view shows while the very first page of results is still loading (before any ticket has appeared)? [Gap, Coverage]
- [ ] CHK020 Are requirements defined for the infinite-scroll failure case (next-page request fails mid-scroll)? [Gap, Coverage, Spec §FR-004a]
- [ ] CHK021 Are requirements defined for resuming/retrying a failed comment or edit submission without losing what the user typed? [Gap, Coverage]
- [x] CHK022 Are requirements defined for what happens to an open edit form if the ticket is transitioned to a terminal status (CLOSED/CANCELLED) by another action while editing is in progress? [Gap, Exception Flow] — Resolved: covered by the general concurrent-modification edge case ("second save... succeed against latest state or fail with the backend's specific error... UI must show whichever specific message the backend returns"), which applies uniformly regardless of the specific interleaving.
- [ ] CHK023 Are requirements defined for keyboard-only completion of each primary flow (search/filter, create, edit, comment, transition)? [Gap, Coverage]
- [ ] CHK024 Are requirements defined for screen-reader announcement of dynamically-appearing content (new comment, infinite-scroll-loaded tickets, error messages)? [Gap, Coverage]

## Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK025 Are requirements defined for extremely long field values (title, description, comment content) and how the UI truncates or wraps them? [Gap, Edge Case]
- [x] CHK026 Are requirements defined for the maximum/typical number of transition options shown at once, and how they're laid out when more than a few are valid from a given status? [Gap, Edge Case] — Resolved: bounded by the domain itself, not by a stated UI rule — Feature 1's fixed state machine (referenced by FR-010) never offers more than 2 next statuses from any given status, so a "many options" layout scenario is structurally impossible under the current state machine.
- [ ] CHK027 Are requirements defined for double-submission prevention (e.g. rapid repeated clicks on create/comment/transition controls)? [Gap, Edge Case]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] CHK028 Are accessibility requirements (e.g. WCAG conformance level, focus management, ARIA roles for dynamic regions) specified anywhere in the spec, or left entirely to planning? [Gap, Non-Functional]
- [x] CHK029 Are requirements defined for how error/empty-state messages are presented consistently (e.g. always via the shared error-display component referenced in FR-015)? [Consistency, Spec §FR-015] — Resolved: FR-015 explicitly mandates one shared error-display component as the presentation surface every error/empty state (FR-012, FR-013, FR-014) routes through.
- [ ] CHK030 Are internationalization/localization requirements (or an explicit exclusion) documented for user-facing text? [Gap, Non-Functional]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK031 Is the assumption that users operate from "a desktop browser" validated against any minimum viewport/breakpoint requirement, or left unspecified? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK032 Is the dependency on the new assignee-list endpoint (FR-005b) reflected as a blocking dependency for User Story 2 and User Story 4, given both require it for their acceptance scenarios? [Dependency, Spec §FR-005b] — Resolved: sequencing execution order is plan/tasks-level, not spec-level, but the dependency itself is unambiguous in the spec (both stories explicitly reference the FR-005a/b-sourced picker), and it was in fact correctly captured as a Phase 2 (foundational, blocking) task in tasks.md.

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [x] CHK033 Is the term "immediately" in FR-009 ("display it ... immediately after it is successfully added") quantified, or could it be read as requiring real-time push vs. a simple post-submit re-render? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-009] — Resolved: SC-006 pins down the mechanism ("without a full page reload"), which rules out the real-time-push reading — it's a client-side re-render after the user's own action, not a latency target or a push/subscription requirement.
- [x] CHK034 Does SC-004's "no offered transition is ever rejected ... under normal, single-user conditions" implicitly assume the UI's transition list is refreshed on every detail-view load — is that assumption stated anywhere? [Ambiguity, Spec §SC-004] — Resolved: User Story 6 Scenario 1 states the transition options are computed "When its detail view is opened" based on "the current status" at that moment, confirming the list is (re)computed fresh on every load, not cached across loads.

## Notes

- **Review pass (2026-09-25, during Phase 5 implementation)**: 14/34 items resolved on a genuine re-read of spec.md's Given/When/Then clauses and cross-references (CHK006, 011–016, 018, 022, 026, 029, 032–034). Each resolution is annotated inline with the specific spec text that resolves it. The remaining 20 unchecked items are real, still-open gaps — mostly accessibility (CHK023, 024, 028), exact UI copy/layout left to implementation by design (CHK002, 003, 004, 005, 007, 008, 009, 010), and edge cases not yet in spec.md (CHK017, 019, 020, 021, 025, 027, 030, 031). None of these block continued implementation; they're candidates for a future `/speckit-clarify` round or explicit "left to implementation" acknowledgment.
- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`

- Link to relevant resources or documentation
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
